historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run container volume growth (~3-4%/yr demand) at mid-cycle rates; every trailing CAGR is distorted by the 2021-22 freight supercycle
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 39.5% vs revenue 5.1% and EPS 19.7%: book value was built by the 2021-22 supercycle windfall (RMB199bn of net profit in two years), not by repeatable compounding. 3yr CAGRs run from the FY2022 peak and are all sharply negative. None is a usable forward growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less interest income; SBC nil). SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs differ only by interest income, which shrank as the cash pile was distributed.

scenario_narratives.base: Freight rates keep falling through FY2027 as ~7% fleet growth meets ~3-4% demand and the Red Sea diversion unwinds; COSCO's volumes still grow with the Ocean Alliance network (extended to 2032) and supply-chain/terminal revenue cushion the trough. Margins revert to a mid-cycle EBITDAaL of ~13% -- below the FY2023-25 average, well above the pre-COVID FY2019 6.8% -- reflecting a more consolidated, alliance-disciplined industry. The newbuild capex hump (RMB52bn) passes by FY2028.
scenario_narratives.bull: The cycle bottoms shallow: Red Sea/Cape routing persists or geopolitical disruption recurs, carriers blank-sail and scrap aggressively, and the green-fleet transition retires older tonnage; COSCO captures share in ASEAN/LatAm/Middle East corridors (Chancay, Sukhna) and grows non-freight supply-chain revenue. Mid-cycle EBITDAaL ~16.7%, near the FY2023-25 run-rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: Overcapacity overwhelms discipline: full Suez transit returns, the record orderbook delivers, and US port fees/Section-301 measures disproportionately hit China-linked carriers on COSCO's largest lane. Rates fall to 2016-type lows in FY2027 and mid-cycle EBITDAaL settles near 8%. The large net cash and associate book keep the equity well above zero -- the bear case is an earnings collapse, not a solvency event. In this path the operating business has a slightly negative enterprise value (PV of explicit flows -RMB13.2bn, terminal capped at 10x a 1.4% FCF margin): the bear IV of ~HK$10.25 is essentially the balance sheet alone (net cash + associates + investments - NCI - interim dividend ~= HK$10.35/share). The zero terminal floor is not hit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cyclical valued through the cycle, not off FY0: explicit trough in FY2027, reversion to a mid-cycle margin, a 12x (bear 10x) terminal cap appropriate to a commodity freight business, and a balance sheet (net cash, associates, investments, less NCI and the declared interim dividend) worth roughly 60% of the share price on its own.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of mid-cycle EBITDAaL margin (FY2029 onward) is worth roughly HK$1.1/share
Surplus-cash assumption: all RMB140.8bn of cash treated as surplus; liners need an operating float
Associates and NCI held at book, not market
US port fees / sanctions specific to Chinese state-linked carriers
Capital allocation: newbuild commitments locked in at the top of the cycle; state-shareholder priorities over minority returns
FX: RMB/HKD rate is dated and not refreshed by price-only updates

Mid-cycle owner-FCF margin (base ~4.9%) assumes capex normalises to 6.5% of revenue after the newbuild hump; post-lease owner FCF was near zero or negative in FY2019, FY2023 and FY2025, so capex discipline is the swing factor

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 12.63-18.04 HKD
data_sources.financials: 1919.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2018-FY2025, H1 FY2026); FY2025 annual report (income statement, note 8 leases, note 31 expenses by nature, cash flow statement); H1 FY2026 interim report (balance sheet at 30 Jun 2026, interim dividend)

inputs.share_count_basis: Shares in issue (A+H) at 30 Jun 2026 per H1 FY2026 interim (15,298.4m); no material dilutive securities. Held FLAT. SBC is ~zero, so the ongoing A/H buybacks (RMB6.56bn FY2025, July-2026 programme RMB7.7-15.4bn authorised) genuinely shrink the count; flat count is therefore conservative.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash flow statement: share-based payment nil (FY2023 RMB9.9m, FY2024 RMB0.3m); no net-share-settlement taxes. SBC-zero market -- house and street coincide.
inputs.fx_note: Model in RMB (CNY) millions; per-share values converted to HKD at 1.1724 HKD per CNY (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16 22:02Z). Cross-check: Yahoo CNY=X 6.6768 and HKD=X 7.8479 imply 1.1754 (0.3% tie). Dual-listing parity: A share 601919.SS RMB16.88 x 1.1724 = HK$19.79 vs H share HK$17.19 -- a 15% A/H premium, normal for this name, so the H-share quote is the right price basis and the direction (RMB -> HKD multiply) is confirmed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: RMB flows, so RMB-built rate: China 10y CGB ~1.9% + beta ~1.15 x ERP ~6.5% = ~9.4% cost of equity; with a large net cash position WACC ~= CoE. 9.5% used in all three scenarios -- freight-cycle, US port-fee and geopolitical risk live in the scenario flows and weights, not in a WACC premium (charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash payment (FY2025 'Payment of lease liabilities' RMB14,513m, which includes the lease interest -- interest paid of RMB1,611m in operating is borrowing interest only, vs lease interest of RMB1,845m in finance costs) deducted via lease_cost_pct_path (6.6% of revenue FY2025). Lease liabilities (RMB41.6bn at 30 Jun 2026) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 total D&A RMB20,990m less RoU depreciation RMB11,418m = RMB9,572m, 4.4% of revenue) so cash-tax EBIT does not charge the lease twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (OOCL/OOIL and COSCO SHIPPING Ports both carry minorities); NCI charged ONCE by deducting the NCI book value RMB51,549m (30 Jun 2026) in the equity bridge. FY2025 NCI took 12.4% of total profit; book is a fair proxy given Ports trades near/below book.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the cyclical/non-US adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'). Container shipping is an operating business, not a financial, so owner-FCF applies, but FY0 is NOT used as a run-rate: the driver paths normalise to a mid-cycle margin. Mid-cycle evidence (EBITDA pre-IFRS16 = operating profit + total D&A, less lease cash = 'EBITDAaL'): FY2019 6.8%, FY2020 10.1%, FY2021 39.7%, FY2022 ~42.6%, FY2023 16.8%, FY2024 27.6%, FY2025 18.7%, H1 FY2026 ~16.7%. Ex the 2021-22 COVID supercycle the average is ~16%; the base mid-cycle EBITDAaL is set at 13% (EBITDA 19.5% less leases 6.5%) because the industry orderbook (~30% of fleet), FY2025 capacity growth ~7% vs demand ~3.5-4%, and Red Sea/Suez normalisation point to a trough in FY2027 before reverting. Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 20,530 - SBC 0 - interest income 5,378 = 15,152; after treatment-(B) lease cash (14,513) it is only ~639, because FY2025 capex (RMB25.0bn, 11.4% of revenue) carries the 54-vessel newbuild programme (RMB52.05bn commitments). Capex is projected elevated through FY2027 and normalises to 6.5% of revenue (above ex-RoU D&A of 5.5%) -- owned newbuilds replace charters, which is why the lease % drifts down slightly. Associates/JVs (RMB77.5bn book; FY2025 share of profit RMB5.24bn, a 6.8% yield on book) and FVOCI investments (RMB4.7bn) are excluded from the flows and added at book in the equity bridge (matching-asset rule); finance income is likewise excluded from the flows and the cash is in net debt. All cash treated as surplus; an operating float of ~RMB10-15bn would cut ~HK$0.8-1.1/share. Buybacks are a distribution, not an SBC offset (SBC-zero market), so band_position is null: house and street collapse to one basis.

bear.narrative: A 2012-16-style glut: full Suez return releases 6-7% of effective capacity onto a record orderbook, US port fees and tariffs hit the Trans-Pacific lane (28% of revenue), FY2027 revenue -14% with EBITDAaL near 2.5%, and mid-cycle settles at ~8% EBITDAaL -- between FY2019 and FY2020.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue -3% (H1 +2.6% YoY but H2 rates weaker), FY2027 the trough (-8%, EBITDA 16% / EBITDAaL ~9%) as Red Sea normalises into an over-ordered fleet, then recovery to a 19.5% EBITDA / 13% EBITDAaL mid-cycle and ~3% volume-led growth.

bull.narrative: Disruption and discipline persist: Red Sea/Cape routing absorbs capacity longer, alliance blank-sailing and scrapping of older tonnage hold rates, supply-chain revenue keeps compounding; mid-cycle EBITDAaL ~16.7%, close to the FY2023-25 average.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% house default because the near-term supply/demand setup is documented (orderbook, Suez normalisation, US port fees) and the base already assumes recovery to a margin above the pre-COVID norm. Base 50% as the central mid-cycle reversion. Bull cut to 20% because it needs disruption or unusual capacity discipline to persist for years, both outside the company's control.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
